lesson.title: Recruitment and worker management
lesson.summary: Identify recruitment and worker-management functions, including targeting, ranking and individual monitoring.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must distinguish a listed-use match from the product route.

blocks: **Recruitment use** includes recruitment or selection of people, particularly targeted job advertisements, analysis/filtering of applications and candidate evaluation.

Northbridge's assistant predicts applicant suitability and ranks applications. Compare that function with point 4(a). A person still choosing interviews does not automatically make a ranking unrelated to selection.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 4(a), 4(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: **Worker-management use** includes decisions affecting work terms, promotion or termination, task allocation based on individual behaviour or traits, and monitoring/evaluation of work performance and behaviour.

An AI assigning work based on an individual's observed behaviour differs from a simple neutral calendar. Record the basis for allocation and how the output affects work, rather than treating all scheduling alike.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 4(a), 4(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: The listed area includes access to self-employment as well as employment and workers' management. A contractor or platform-worker label should not end the intended-purpose comparison.
For each function, identify the affected person, personal inputs, output and decision context. Other employment and personal-data rules need their own checks.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 4(a), 4(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: Fictional changed case: Northbridge first uses a tool only to convert application files. It later adds suitability predictions and shortlists. Reassess the actual new function.

A limited processing function and an evaluative selection function have different evidence. The later derogation module tests whether a listed use qualifies; it does not automatically exempt every tool called administrative.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 4(a), 4(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)
